title: Agreement of the finite coefficient and cocone tensor comparisons
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $X$ any scheme, and $E\subseteq H\subseteq\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ finite intermediate extensions. Use the internal coefficient rings and canonical derived extension, restriction, adjunction and tensor comparison data of [def-weil-pbc-finite-derived-tensor-comparison]; in particular $\underline\Omega$ consists of continuous functions with image in one finite subfield. Identify the finite and algebraic-closure extension functors with [def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield] and [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar], respectively: both are total left derived extension along the same coefficient inclusions. Under these identifications the fixed comparison $\theta_{E,H}:T_{H,\Omega}T_{E,H}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{E,\Omega}$ is the canonical comparison of [def-sfb-derived-extend-comp-iso]. On the bounded constructible full subcategories, both its forward and inverse components are exactly the ambient arrows underlying the corresponding components of [def-sfb-constructible-extend-comp-iso]. This asserts equality of the specified comparisons, not merely existence of some natural isomorphism.

source.place: Exact-derived composition comparison and the canonical underived extension comparison; applied to the Hom-surj transitivity sentence

proof.text: The definitions finiteCoefficientDerivedTensorCompIso and derivedExtendScalarsCompIso have the same body, including the exact-derived composition isomorphism, the underived scalar-extension comparison, and the coefficient-map equality. Their endpoints agree definitionally by finiteCoefficientDerivedExtension, finiteCoefficientDerivedToAlgCl, derivedExtendScalarsSubfield and derivedExtendScalarsToPadicAlgCl. Prove equality of the specified natural isomorphisms by reflexivity. No adjunction uniqueness theorem is needed.

For each bounded constructible object K, unfold constructibleToPadicAlgClCompIso and replace the ambient comparison by the definitionally equal finiteCoefficientDerivedTensorCompIso. Apply Functor.fullyFaithfulCancelRight_hom_app and Functor.fullyFaithfulCancelRight_inv_app. Rewrite each underlying full-subcategory arrow backwards with ObjectProperty.ι_map, then apply Functor.map_preimage. This recovers the ambient components without reconstructing their coefficient-ring instances. The forward component has an identity on the left, removed by Category.id_comp; the inverse component has an identity on the right, removed by Category.comp_id. This gives both required component equalities.

proof_origin.place: Literal equality of the two existing comparison definitions; full-subcategory restriction as in def-sfb-constructible-extend-comp-iso.proof.md. Lean proof by reflexivity, fullyFaithfulCancelRight component equations, ObjectProperty.ι_map, map_preimage, and the category identity laws (E2, 2026-10-21).

lean.statement: theorem finiteCoefficient_cocone_comparison_agreement (X : Scheme.{u}) (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] {E H : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ} (h : E ≤ H) : finiteCoefficientDerivedTensorCompIso X ℓ h = derivedExtendScalarsCompIso X ℓ h ∧ ∀ K : PadicSubfieldConstructible X ℓ E, ((constructibleToPadicAlgClCompIso X ℓ h).hom.app K).hom = (finiteCoefficientDerivedTensorCompIso X ℓ h).hom.app K.obj ∧ ((constructibleToPadicAlgClCompIso X ℓ h).inv.app K).hom = (finiteCoefficientDerivedTensorCompIso X ℓ h).inv.app K.obj
